hook.line: Everyone in La Candelaria has a theory about whether Altamira will really get the block, and Tomás is tired of being asked. Sometimes the honest answer is neither yes nor no: you doubt it, or it might happen. Spanish has a verb form for that.
hook.es: Dudo que Altamira cambie de idea.
hook.en: I doubt Altamira will change his mind.

examples.es: Dudo que Altamira cambie de idea.
examples.en: I doubt Altamira will change his mind.
You may be right. (to a friend)
I doubt Vale is coming today.

examples.es: Es posible que Mariana sepa algo.

examples.en: I don't doubt you're right. (to a friend)
Do you doubt they'll come? (to a friend)

rule:
Look at the verb after *que*: *cambie*, *llueva*, *tengas*, *venga*. It is the wish form you already know from *quiero que* and *no creo que*.

Three frames lead to it:
*Dudo que* + wish form
*Es posible que* + wish form
*Puede que* + wish form

The idea is simple. If you doubt something, or it is only possible, you are not putting it on the table as a fact, so the verb steps back.

The flip side: *No dudo que* means you are sure, so the plain verb comes back: *No dudo que tienes razón*.

English never changes the verb here (I doubt he comes, I doubt he's coming). In Spanish, spot the doubt word and switch.
smallPrint: Teachers call this the subjunctive after expressions of doubt and possibility. *No dudo que* is certainty, so it takes the indicative.

options: I doubt Vale is coming today.
I know Vale is coming today.
I hope Vale comes today.
It rained today.
It's raining today for sure.
It might rain today.
I don't doubt you're right. (to a friend)
I doubt you're right. (to a friend)
I hope you're right. (to a friend)
Mariana knows something for sure.
Mariana might know something.

readAndPick.es: Dudo que mi abuela lo sepa.
options: I'm sure my grandmother knows it.
I think my grandmother knew it.
I doubt my grandmother knows it.

readAndPick.es: No dudo que Altamira quiere comprar el barrio.
options: I doubt Altamira wants to buy the neighbourhood.
I'm sure Altamira wants to buy the neighbourhood.
Altamira might want to buy the neighbourhood.
I doubt they want to sell.
I doubt we want to sell.
I doubt you want to sell. (to a friend)
They might have money tomorrow.
We might have money tomorrow.
I have money tomorrow for sure.

readAndPick.es: Es posible que el café esté abierto.
options: The café is open for sure.
The café was open.
The café might be open.

yourTurn.prompt: Pick *venga* or *viene* and type the whole sentence: *Dudo que Vale ___ hoy.*
yourTurn.why: After *dudo que* the verb takes the wish form: *venga*.

yourTurn.prompt: Pick *tienes* or *tengas* and type the whole sentence, to a friend: *Puede que ___ razón.*
yourTurn.why: *Puede que* means it is only possible, so the wish form: *tengas*.

yourTurn.prompt: Pick *tienes* or *tengas* and type the whole sentence, to a friend: *No dudo que ___ razón.*
yourTurn.why: *No dudo que* means you are sure, so the plain verb comes back: *tienes*.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: I doubt Altamira will change his mind.
yourTurn.answer: Dudo que Altamira cambie de idea.
yourTurn.why: *Dudo que* is followed by the wish form of *cambiar*: *cambie*.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: It might rain today.
yourTurn.why: Both *es posible que* and *puede que* say it is possible, and both take *llueva*.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: Mariana might know something.
yourTurn.answer: Es posible que Mariana sepa algo.
yourTurn.why: A possibility, so the wish form of *saber*: *sepa*.

yourTurn.prompt: Make it a doubt: *Mi abuela lo sabe.* Start with *Dudo que*.
yourTurn.answer: Dudo que mi abuela lo sepa.
yourTurn.why: Once you start with *dudo que*, *sabe* becomes *sepa*.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: I doubt they want to sell.

pitfalls.why: Almost. English keeps the same verb after doubt, but Spanish switches to the wish form after *dudo que*.
Almost. *No dudo que* means you are sure, so there is nothing to step back from: the plain verb stays.
Almost. *Es posible que* only says it might happen, so the verb takes the wish form.

personal: Say one thing you doubt about this week, starting with *Dudo que*. Then say one thing that might happen, starting with *Es posible que* or *Puede que*.
